svg.title: The GIOP header, and why the byte order matters
svg.desc: The 12-byte GIOP header of frame 19 of corba.pcap, a little-endian Request inside a MIOP datagram: magic GIOP, version 1.2, flags 01, type 0 (Request), message size D8 00 00 00. Bit 0 of the flags says little-endian, so the size is 216 bytes. Read big-endian, as the first version of the parser did, the same bytes say 3623878656 and the message was rejected.
